d.description:
eCash is a Bitcoin hard fork initiated by Bitcoin developer Paul Sztorc. The project aims to preserve Bitcoin's core architecture while introducing native support for Drivechains (BIP-300) and additional Layer 2 functionality.

The network is designed as a near-copy of Bitcoin Core, using the SHA-256 proof-of-work algorithm and maintaining compatibility with the existing Bitcoin software stack wherever practical. Bitcoin holders will be able to claim eCash on a 1:1 basis after the fork.

The project's objective is to provide an alternative Bitcoin-compatible network focused on experimentation with scalability, programmable sidechains, and protocol development while preserving the familiar Bitcoin user experience.

eCash is an open-source project. Development is led by Paul Sztorc, the creator of the Drivechain proposal, with source code, technical documentation, and development updates published publicly. The project seeks to enable innovation through optional Layer 2 networks while maintaining a simple and transparent Layer 1 protocol.
d.short_description: eCash is a Bitcoin hard fork that preserves its core architecture while adding native support for BIP-300

d.description:
Arc is an open Layer-1 blockchain designed to provide an enterprise-grade foundation for stablecoin payments, FX, and capital markets applications. The EVM-compatible network features USDC as its native gas, along with an integrated stablecoin FX engine, sub-second settlement finality, and opt-in privacy controls. Arc will be fully integrated across Circle’s platform and services, which will also remain fully available and interoperable with the dozens of other partner blockchains that Circle supports.

Featuring:

  • USDC as native gas

  • Built-in FX engine

  • Deterministic sub-second finality

  • Opt-in privacy

  • Full Circle platform integration

At its core is Malachite, a high-performance consensus engine developed by Informal Systems that powers Arc with safety, liveness, and resilience at scale.

Arc expands the design space for stablecoins by uniting speed with certainty and delivering the native tooling needed to meet real-world business obligations. Open and composable, Arc is designed to interoperate seamlessly with the broader multichain ecosystem. Fully EVM-compatible, developers will be able to build on Arc using the same frameworks and tooling they know and trust.

It incentivizes reporting of quantum vulnerabilities through emissions and creates a mechanism to distribute attack costs via verifiable proofs. d.description:
Primus (formerly known as PADO Labs) is a decentralized trust, verification, and privacy layer designed to bridge the gap between Web2 data and the Web3 agent economy. The Primus Network leverages advanced cryptographic techniques—specifically zero-knowledge Transport Layer Security (zkTLS) and zero-knowledge Fully Homomorphic Encryption (zkFHE)—to enable secure, permissionless data attestation. This infrastructure allows developers to bring arbitrary off-chain data and API responses on-chain in a highly secure and verifiable manner without compromising user privacy.

Currently operating on its decentralized AlphaNet, Primus provides the foundational cryptography needed for verifiable AI agent execution, confidential financial services, and trusted credit protocols. By unifying data, state, and action verification into a single execution layer, the platform enables smart contracts and autonomous AI models to securely process real-world information. This architecture effectively mitigates the traditional oracle problem, establishing a robust environment for decentralized finance and the emerging DeFAI ecosystem.

d.description:
ActionModel develops a community-owned Large Action Model (LAM), an AI system designed to perform real digital tasks on computers by interacting with graphical user interfaces (GUIs), rather than just generating text like traditional Large Language Models (LLMs). It observes screen states, decides on actions (such as clicking coordinates, typing, or scrolling) using a proprietary Action Tree built from user contributions, executes those actions, and loops until the task completes. This enables autonomous automation of workflows like data entry, web navigation, or app operations without relying on APIs.

The project counters centralized AI development by Big Tech through community contributions: users install a browser extension for passive or active training and build/sell reusable workflows on a marketplace where executions generate ongoing rewards for creators.

The Actionist desktop app serves as the user-facing tool, allowing creation of specialized AI agents (digital employees with memory, schedules, personalities, and tool access) that run locally or in the cloud for 24/7 operation, with full history tracking for transparency.

$LAM is the native token that powers actions, rewards training and contributions, enables governance, and represents ownership stakes in the AI system.

d.description: Reflect Protocol is a decentralized finance (DeFi) platform on the Solana blockchain that enables users to create and redeem digital representations of international currencies, known as Reflected Digital Currencies (RDCs). By depositing liquid staking tokens (LSTs) as collateral, users can mint RDCs like US Dollar Reflected (USDR) at a 1:1 value, facilitating a delta-neutral position that mitigates exposure to cryptocurrency price volatility. The protocol generates yield through a combination of native staking rewards from the Solana network and funding rate income from perpetual futures markets. To safeguard user deposits, Reflect employs an insurance fund comprising both cash reserves and validated restaked assets, ensuring a minimum insurance ratio relative to assets under management. Additionally, Reflect operates its own validator node on Solana, contributing to network security and earning staking rewards that are distributed to participants. The protocol emphasizes transparency and decentralization, providing open-source tools and documentation for developers to integrate its services into various decentralized applications.

At its core, the protocol employs an ERC-721 standard for creating digital twin tokens that link physical items to verified vaults and shops, ensuring tamper-proof custody and authenticity proofs; the RWE Oracle aggregates live data from global markets, custodians, and sentiment indicators to deliver manipulation-resistant fair market value (FMV) and current market value (CMV) benchmarks; and the RLP Vault enables programmable trading, DeFi lending, auctions, and automated strategies on these tokenized assets, transforming static collectibles into yield-generating, instantly tradable RWAs without logistics hurdles.

Key features include a Gacha Machine Aggregator for transparent, on-chain blind box sales with provable fairness and immediate liquidity; an instant marketplace for seamless peer-to-peer trades; and integrations with institutional custodians for insured storage, bridging offline verification with on-chain composability to foster a unified ecosystem where users stake, borrow against, or liquidate collectibles like a "Bloomberg Terminal for the collectible economy."

d.description:
At its core, Phantom works by creating and managing private keys on behalf of its users. These keys can then be used within Phantom to store funds and sign transactions.

Developers can interact with Phantom via both web applications as well as iOS and Android applications.

To interact with web applications, the Phantom extension and mobile in-app browser injects a phantom object into the javascript context of every site the user visits. A given web app may then interact with Phantom, and ask for the user's permission to perform transactions, through this injected provider.

It's also possible to interact with the Phantom mobile app through universal links and deeplinks. With deeplinks, mobile apps can prompt their users to connect, sign, and send with Phantom directly. Once complete, Phantom will redirect users back to their referring applications.
